column1: # One verdict per published Gmail API method. Held by `go run ./scripts/gates api-coverage`.
# Columns: method id, state, phase, verdict. The verb and path live in testdata/api-surface.json.
# used: a client call exists (internal/gapi). planned: judged used or gated, built in the named phase (§16).
# out: deferred or written off; the verdict says why.

column4: Used: `create_draft`, including replies (§4.5); a multipart upload above 5 MB (§7.4). Never repeated after an ambiguous failure
Used: `delete_draft`, with `confirm: true`. Permanent, but only ever an unsent draft; decided in §17.1 not to sit behind the destructive flag
Used: `get_draft`, and the witness read before `update_draft` (§4.4)
Gated: `send_draft`, registered only with `GMAIL_ENABLE_SEND=true`, behind the recipient guard; never retried; an ambiguous outcome is settled by reading (§4.3)
Used: `update_draft`. PUT-only and no ETag; guarded by the message-id witness of §4.4, a recorded deviation (§17b); a multipart upload above 5 MB
Used: `get_profile`; also the login email lookup and `doctor`'s probe
Used: `create_label`, the name checked against the label list first (§6.2)
Gated: `delete_label`, behind `GMAIL_ENABLE_DESTRUCTIVE` with `confirm: true`; it strips the label from every message and cannot be undone
Used: `list_labels` with `counts: true` (list omits the counts)
Used: `update_label`; only the fields given are sent (§4.4)
Written off: PUT replaces the whole label; `patch` covers every edit (§4.4)

Written off: "provides no guarantees that messages were not already deleted or even existed", so its result cannot be reported truthfully; `delete_permanently` loops `messages.delete` under a cap instead

Written off: it answers with no body, so it cannot say which messages changed or why one failed, and §4.7 reports per item. `modify_labels` calls `messages.modify` per message, 5 units each, whose answer is the message's labels after (§18 row 39)
Gated: `delete_permanently`, registered only with `GMAIL_ENABLE_DESTRUCTIVE=true`, with `confirm: true`; the only scope it accepts is `https://mail.google.com/`
Used: `get_message`, `download_attachment` (to find the part), reply construction (to read `Message-ID`/`References`)
Written off: mailbox migration, not an assistant task; it runs spam and virus classification as though delivered
Written off for the server: it plants mail that was never delivered, bypassing the classification a received message gets. Used by the live driver only, to write the messages it reads (§9.1)
Used: `modify_labels`, once per message, its answer the labels after
Written off: sending goes through `drafts.send` only, so what leaves is always something that existed as a draft the person could see (§4.2); `send_draft` covers every case a one-shot send would
Written off: client-side encryption is Workspace-admin key management; an encrypted body is unreadable through this API regardless
Written off with CSE: permanent key destruction
Written off: grants another person the mailbox; `gmail.settings.sharing`
Written off: delegation is account administration; `gmail.settings.basic`
Deferred (§17): a filter's `action.forward` is auto-forwarding by another route; buildable only with forward refused structurally
Written off: `filters.list` returns every field `get` does, for the same one unit, and an account holds at most 1,000 filters; `list_filters` reads the list (§18 row 36)
Written off: `gmail.settings.sharing`, which this server never requests
Written off: `forwardingAddresses.list` returns every field `get` does, for the same one unit; `get_settings` reads the list (§18 row 36)
Used: `get_settings` (read, so a person can see whether mail is leaving)
Written off: `sendAs.list` returns every field `get` does for the same one unit, and `create_draft` reads the list anyway for the default sender and the account's own addresses (§18 row 39)
Written off: `gmail.settings.basic`/`sharing`; signature editing is deferred to §17
Written off: uploads a private key
Written off: turning forwarding on sends all future mail elsewhere; the single most dangerous write this API offers to an injected instruction (§4.1)
Written off: client-protocol configuration, not an assistant task
Written off: display preference, no assistant task
Deferred (§17): an auto-reply writes to every sender, so it is sending by another name and needs its own argument
Written off: push goes to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic, which a stdio process cannot own or receive. `list_changes` polls `history.list` instead
